fixed.item: breakages.json row 24 (navigation_robot): layout_audit --gen 2 domain follow-ups -- a robot-vacuum dock's keep-clear zone left targets reachable only over hazards (seed 25 couple_with_infant living_room_1: the dock's own outlet wall_outlet_5 boxed in by the zone and a plugged-in tower fan placed earlier by climate.fans, which the placement rule set aside as a loose thing; seed 27 multigenerational office_1: electrical.hookup (order 97) mounted wall_outlet_26/27 on the zone's wall after the dock was placed, falling back from hazard-free wall cells)
fixed.how: furnish.py: new generation-2-only furnisher navigation_robot.dock_check (order 120, after every other furnisher, its own stream; returns at once in generation 1, so gen-1 houses and draws are untouched). It judges each household-robot dock's zone in the finished house against every floor hazard (_zone_cuts_nothing(every_hazard=True): loose things too, the rings of people asleep in bed left out as the layout audit does; the robots seated on the dock ignored). A dock whose zone cuts a hazard-free route or the only hazard-free access to anything is moved, with the robots seated on it, to the first outlet spot that cuts nothing (_dock_at_outlet(every_hazard=True): its own room first, then VACUUM_ROOMS); it keeps its id and record (placement and plug fields only, a cord run the hookup laid for it is lifted); with no such spot the dock and its robots are removed, as when no room had a spot at first. A dock whose zone cuts nothing is not touched (byte-identical). layout_audit.py 30 --gen 2 --domain navigation_robot: 330 houses, 0 problems, 0 domain follow-ups (was 2); gen-2 notes unchanged (709). Over all 233 generation-2 authored specs x 15 seeds (0 1 2 41 97 and 501-510) the furnisher changes 0 of 3,495 builds, so no spec world changes

fixed.item: Forced realistic + geometric run of T-5ad61b6881821b-01 (seeds 1, 41, variant 0; failing on the pre-change snapshot too): its wrong plans' 'go_to dock' was refused ('That is not visible here'), so under NeverActed they were no evidence. Root cause in go_to: it resolves a fixed thing on the robot's map (its own dock) as known, but the final core approach needs the thing in view, and the geometric camera cannot make a dock plate out from where the robot enters a dim room (camera.can_see is position-based: turning the head does not help) -- an agent could not 'go_to dock' from another room under the geometric camera
fixed.how: paths.go_to: with the geometric camera, an entity target in the room it arrived in that the robot knows (go_to's _resolve) but cannot see is walked to by the map first (_near_known: core walk_to adjacent with the go_to's avoid and speed, so every hazard applies), then approached; still not in view there, the approach refuses as before. People and pets, social walks and the room camera are untouched (no extra leg; the room-camera golden dump is unchanged)
